Question/Consideration:
Question 1, BEC 20155

Please provide the approval of variation from country of origin.

Please provide the justification letter for the changes.

Please provide justification to show that parameters is non-significant for deletion of a non-significant in process test.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1

The EMA approval for this change (BEC 20155) is pending and expected December 10th, 2021.

Justification:
In-process DNA impurity content testing at the formulated membrane adsorber eluate (MAEF) stage at the end of the cell culture/isolation process is a redundant test point that will be removed from the testing plan. DNA impurity content will continue to be tested at a later point in the process at the membrane adsorption/viral filtrate stage; this is the release testing point for the drug substance for DNA impurity content (see figure below for clarification).
MAEF DNA impurity content testing was initially implemented to support validation run characterization. Testing has continued into commercial operations to better understand long term process behavior. Data collected to date show that the cell culture process is well designed and controlled, generating low levels of DNA impurity that are readily removed by an excess of clearance capacity available in the purification process.

Further, MAEF DNA impurity content results are not used to guide the process downstream of that point (e.g., to make decisions regarding staging of MAEF material for the purification process).

Thus, MAEF DNA impurity content is a non-significant in-process test parameter that can be removed from the testing plan.

Additional detailed justification showing that the MAEF DNA impurity content test is a non-significant in-process test can be found in submitted document S.2.4.10_022958447_01.

Source:
S.2.4.10-01 Damoctocog alfa pegol solution, Control of Critical Steps and Intermediates - Additional Information (DocID: S.2.4.10_022958447_01; unchanged)

Question/Consideration: Please clarify the activities of the Hubertus Apotheke Am Salzufer, Salzufer 13 – 14, 10587 Berlin site, whose MIA and GMP certificate have been provided; please update the IMPD including such activities.
Answer/Response:
The entity Hubertus Apotheke am Salzufer, Salzufer 13/14, 10587 Berlin, Germany will serve as an EU Central Pharmacy, i.e. as central distribution point for study participants enrolled at clinical sites in countries of the European Union. The EU Central Pharmacy is contracted by Thermofisher Scientific who will manage the order processing and logistics to distribute the study medication (IMP and placebo). The EU Central Pharmacy holds the following licenses:
• Public Pharmacy,
• Manufacturing & Importation Authorization (MIA),
• GMP for IMP,
• GMP commercial medicinal products,
• Wholesale distributor,
• Global Distribution Practice (GDP), and
• Direct to Patient - Mail order.
In accordance with EMA/CHMP/QWP/545525/2017 Guideline on the requirements for the chemical and pharmaceutical quality documentation concerning investigational medicinal products in clinical trials distribution points are not necessary to be provided in the IMPD section. Accordingly, information about the EU Central Pharmacy has not been incorporated into the IMPD but has been reflected in the CTAF.
Direct-to-Patient (DtP)-shipments of study medication are offered as a voluntary alternative to on-site dispensation. The shipments are optional and dependent on each participant’s preference and active agreement – documented by giving informed consent to this service. The service is offered in partnership with Thermofisher Scientific and is supported by the Interactive Web Response System (IWRS).
This approach aims at improving participant’s experience and product compliance in the study. The shipments will ease the burden of storage of large size study medication kits (boxes of 270 x 135 x 75 mm) containing monthly supply (60 capsules) which currently require refrigerated storage conditions (2-8°C). Instead of receiving 3 kits of study medication on week 16 during the on-site visit at T4 (after which the next is a phone visit at T5) and storing them at once in the fridge at home, the study participant will receive one kit at site at T4 followed by monthly shipments until T6 containing one kit each. In practice, the participant will store only one kit at a time in the fridge, minimizing potential inconvenience but more importantly possible inadequate storage conditions if such large amount is not feasible to be stored under refrigerated conditions at the particpiant´s home.
DtP-shipment orders are triggered by trained and delegated site staff using IWRS. The orders follow the study drug dispensation schedule as per the study protocol. Shipment orders are sent by delegated site staff including the respective participant´s delivery address to a dedicated mailbox of Thermofisher Scientific Global Helpdesk who subsequently provides order details to the EU Central Pharmacy for dispatch. The order contains coded kit assignment for a respective study participant; however, the EU Central Pharmacy is blinded to treatment type. The courier picks up the kit from the EU Central Pharmacy and after confirmation on compliance with the required storage condition (2-8°C measured with a temperature tracker) delivers the kit to the study participant personally. Delivery steps are recorded in IWRS by Thermofisher Scientific and site staff is informed about successful or unsuccessful delivery via e-mail notifications.

Question/Consideration: S.3.1 - Please provide the documentation supporting the assignment of absolute configurations of both chiral centers in the molecule.
Answer/Response:
The absolute configuration is controlled by the chemical synthesis.
The two building blocks 7479 (highlighted in red color) and 7478 (highlighted in green color) are synthesized using the amino acid (R)-Serine. Both building blocks are tested for chiral purity at release. No racemization or epimerization is observed during the chemical synthesis. Due to the Cahn–Ingold–Prelog (CIP) sequence rules the configuration of BAY 3427080 is 7S and 9aS. The starting material 7483 and the final BAY 3427080 drug substance are tested for chiral purity and diastereomeric purity.
In a single crystal X-ray study the crystal structure was solved and the relative configuration of the drug substance BAY 3427080 was confirmed.

The product temperature at the endpoint of drying in <Step 2> Granulation Process (Site

manufacturing process performed at Garbagnate site.

validation of the manufacturing process at Garbagnate site has shown that with the control range

are within the acceptance criteria of the in-process control (Table 3, T.08.19#006507572_02, 
Validation of the Manufacturing Process/ Rivaroxaban coated tablet 2.5 mg (Site Garbagnate)).

Due to the above mentioned reasons, we believe that it is appropriate to set this parameter as 
range for Garbagnate site.

Question/Consideration:
1) If you already have information for PDE values used for intrauterine formulations notified
by foreign regulatory agencies, foreign pharmacopoeias, etc, please explain its’ detail. If
you already discuss this topic with foreign regulatory agencies, provide the overview of
discussion.
Answer/Response:
In the ICH Q3D guideline the described routes for administration are oral, parenteral and
inhalation. In Bayer Oy we have chosen to perform the evaluation on Elemental impurities for
our drug products as per PDEs defined for parenteral preparations. This approach is actually
mentioned as a basis for other routes of administration in the ICH guideline also.
Bayer Oy is producing both intrauterine delivery systems and implants. Both use same basic
technology of active ingredient release through a polymer matrix. The implants are clearly
assessed as parenteral drug products, hence the chosen approach of evaluating elemental
impurities can be supported also by this fact. According to our opinion for the intrauterine
formulations no stricter PDE limits can be applied as to our implant products. Route of
possible residual elemental impurities into blood circulation is more restricted in case of our
intrauterine products as it is for our Levonorgestrel implant. Please see also Bayer Response
to Question 001-2).

According to our knowledge there are no set PDE values specifically to intrauterine
formulations in any pharmacopoeias, guidelines, standards etc. However, the approach of
utilizing parenteral PDE limits for our intrauterine formulations has been approved by other
Health Authorities worldwide, including all other ICH countries, as no Deficiency Letters
concerning this issue have been received from any Health Authority. Bayer AG's global SOP
also instructs to use the parenteral PDE values for vaginal products. We assume that our
intrauterine systems can be regarded as similar products with vaginal preparations with regard
to Elemental Impurities assessment. Due to the lack of requests for additional data concerning
the approach chosen by Bayer Oy the Elemental Impurity assessment based on parenteral
PDE values can be seen to be appropriate, and also approved by the Health Authorities
worldwide.

No residual elemental impurities have been detected in Mirena IUS, hence, they are on safe
level in the product irrespective of the PDE values applied. Parenteral PDE values, however,
can be assessed appropriate for use in case of an intrauterine formulation.

Please see also Bayer Response to Question 001-3.

The ICH Q3D guide does not define PDE values for other routes of administration other than
oral, inhalation and parenteral. However, in section 3.2 of the ICH Q3D guideline it is
recommended to evaluate the bioavailability of the element via the intended route of
administration and compare this to the bioavailability of the element by the route with an
established PDE. If a difference is observed, a correction factor can be applied to an
established PDE.

A notification received from the ICH Q3D expert working group (EWG) considers mucosa as
a different route from dermal administration. In biological terms it is a different tissue
illustrated by the fact that mucosal applications (e.g. solutions, ointments, suppositories) are
used to facilitate systemic exposure. The uppermost layers both in gastrointestinal track and in
uterus can be regarded as quite similar mucosal tissues. The parenteral PDE has therefore
been considered as the most appropriate way for derivation of a PDE. With this approach an

Question/Consideration:
3) ICH-Q3D Guidelines show how to consider the case that sufficient safety data is not
available with usage of modifying factor which takes into account bioavailability in 
Section 3. 
Taking this into account, from viewpoint of local effects (local irritation, adverse effects at 
the site of administration, etc.), please explain that there is no safety concerns if the PDE 
value is below than PDE value for the injection. 
In Japan, the ICH-Q3D  guideline implementation to existing products is in the grace 
period. Therefore, it is not necessary to conclude the appropriate PDE for this product 
during this review period. If you are still assessing it for this product, please provide rough 
timeline for your assessment.
Answer/Response:
The PDE represents a substance-specific dose that is unlikely to cause an adverse effect if an
individual is exposed at or below this dose every day for a lifetime. Endometrium is assumed
to comprise a rate limiting barrier similar to the intestinal mucous membrane after oral
administration. It can therefore be assumed that an intrauterine application does not lead to
higher amounts of elemental impurities absorbed than by oral application which might even
justify the use of oral PDE values for Mirena.
Nevertheless, a conservative route-to-route extrapolation can be performed by assuming
100% bioavailability of the contaminant. Therefore parenteral PDE values considering a
100% bioavailability of the elemental impurity are used as a worst case scenario. Parenteral
PDE values are much lower than oral PDEs for most of the elemental impurities and therefore
an additional safety margin is provided.
In addition, based on the fact that analytical data prove the absence of elemental impurities in
all analyzed samples of Mirena no safety concern can be expected to exist.

Furthermore, taking into account that an intrauterine system is intended to remain 5 years in
the uterus still additional safety margin is added, i.e. Mirena is administered as only one dose
in 5 years, also with respect to Elemental Impurity residues. Hence, the amount of Elemental
Impurities possibly available for absorption, as well as for causing local effects, is really non-
significant or non-existing.

The conclusion made by Bayer Oy is to apply the parenteral PDE values for it's
Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery systems. This conclusion is supported also by the
feedbacks from other Health Authorities with no requests for additional data and/or
clarifications on any of the 3 IUS products in the global market for which the parenteral PDE
values have been applied to.

Question/Consideration: (5) <IPC 3>  Please consider whether it is necessary to register the number of samples to be tested.
Answer/Response:
The In-Process Control for filling weight <IPC 3>, is operated automatically in two different modes. At the beginning of the production run of each batch, a 100% mode is applied. During this period, each filling point respectively each vial/bottle is checked for dosing. This mode is applied until the filling weight constantly complies with the requirements. All samples taken during the 100% mode are separated from the manufactured batch and are discarded.
Once a constant weight value is achieved for the vials/bottles, the mode is switched to a continuous sampling mode where each filling needle is tested one after another during routine production. The number of samples depends on the speed of the filling line and therefore cannot be defined specifically.
The results are generated to a report and are part of the Batch Record.
In addition, every vial/bottle is routinely checked for the filling level during the optical inspection (100% dosage control).

Question/Consideration: (6) Please explain how do you confirm and manage the sealability and consider register it as an in-process control.
Answer/Response:
The integrity of vials/bottles is assured by testing the torque power of filled vials and bottles during routine production on every batch as an In-Process Control <IPC 3> where the resistance of the cap against an applied twisting force is determined. An adequate torque power is essential for an effective sealing of the containers and to prevent leaking of the drug product. A minimum torque power of ≥10 Ncm for vials (20 mL filling volume) and ≥ 60 Ncm for bottles (50 mL - 250 mL) is specified to assure a tight crimping of the containers.
Values below the specified torque power indicate an insufficient closure of the containers and a potential risk for leakage.
Relevant P.3.3.01 documents were updated to reflect the In-Process Control <IPC 3> for torque measurement. It should be emphasized that this is not a change in the control strategy itself because this measurement is implemented in the standard manufacturing process. Indeed, regulatory documents were updated to correctly reflect the actual manufacturing process.
After sterilization, an optical control is implemented to detect failures before final release of the filled vials/bottles. For release and at the end of shelf life, the integrity is tested by sterility testing, as described in respective specifications P.5.1.01 and P.5.1.02.
Moreover, reports are available for all Iopamiron container closure systems demonstrating the container closure integrity by a microbiological method (please refer to P.2.4.910).

Question/Consideration: Please provide a discussion on the potential genotoxic impurities for the drug substance intermediate EOB-DTPA as per ICH M7.
Answer/Response:
Please find the toxicological qualification reports for impurities in EOB-DTPA. The outcome from the assessment of their genotoxicity can be summarized as follows:
ZK 119930 (HOB-DTPA): Not present in the final Drug Product, and therefore not subject of toxicological analysis.
ZK 226899 (EOB-EDTA): Not present in the final Drug Product, and therefore not subject of toxicological analysis.
ZK 131897 (Gd-HOB-DTPA): The results did not reveal a potential of Gd-EOB-DTPA (ZK 139834) or the impurities contained in the batch to induce DNA damage. Since all these studies did not indicate any mutagenic/genotoxic/ potential even at maximum tested doses/concentrations, the impurity ZK 131897 was considered as toxicologically qualified also with regard to this endpoint.
ZK 208983 (Ca-EOB-EDTA): the genotoxic potential of ZK 208983 was tested in vitro using the Ames Test and the Chromosomal Aberration Test. On the basis of the negative results obtained in both test systems the market formulation spiked with the impurity ZK 208983 at a level of 2.34% was considered to be non-mutagenic.

In addition, Primovist as well as the impurities (incl. ZK 131897 and ZK 208983) contained in the test batch were considered to be non-effective in the in-vivo/in-vitro UDS-test, i.e. they failed to induce DNA-damage leading to increased DNA-repair in-vitro and in-vivo.
ZK 00215847 (dimethyl ester of EOB-DTPA): Not present in the final Drug Product, and therefore not subject of toxicological analysis.

Specificity:
The degradation experiments performed during the validation of the method for assay and 
impurities were aimed to prove the selectivity and specificity of the method. It had to be 
shown, that all potential degradation products which were formed during the different stress 
tests were separated from the active ingredient and from each other. For this purpose, it is not 
necessary to quantify the amount of each degradation product because the amount of a 
degradation product does not directly have an influence on the specificity.
The thermal stress test results are presented in P.8.3.04, the photostability stress test results 
are reported in P.8.3.05. Both with quantitative results. Chromatograms of temperature 
stressed samples showing that all potential degradation products are well separated from 
vericiguat and from each other are presented on page 22 of the validation report P.5.3.01, 
therefore specificity was shown for temperature related degradation products. The light stress 
test reported in P.8.3.05 did not yield any degradation product above the reporting threshold. 
Therefore specificity is not an issue with degradation products caused by light.
The amount of degradation products for the oxidative and chemically stressed sample 
solutions are presented directly in the chromatograms shown in the validation report P.5.3.01 
(pages 24 – 27).

Linearity:
The acceptance criterion r ≥ 0.98 is not a specification. However, we understand that for UV 
detection the linear range is several magnitudes, and the precision with UV detection is also 
good. Therefore, we agree that the acceptance criterion for the correlation coefficient could 
have been set to be at least 0.990 instead of 0.98.
However, the validation yielded a result of r = 1.000 for vericiguat in the range of 0.05% to 
150%. The linearity of the method is therefore proven to be excellent and even more strict 
acceptance criteria would be met.

- Additional historical data for ampoules up to 60 months for 7 batches (P.8.3.01#018693553_01)
The available stability data for Sulprostone solution 0.5 mg for injection (NALADOR) in vials have been subjected to a statistical analysis for the test items “Assay” and “Sum of all degradation products” to verify the proposed shelf-life as outlined in document P.8.1.02 “Shelf Life”. By the stability data obtained so far at long-term and at accelerated storage conditions, and with the statistical evaluation, the already known stability behavior for Sulprostone lyophilizate 0.5 mg for injection in vials is supported.

The statistical analysis of stability parameters of “Assay” and “Sum of all degradation products” stored at 5 °C at 25 °C identifies that the product is unaffected by the primary packaging container (ampoule and vial).

Moreover, the stability data under accelerated conditions of 25ºC / 60% RH for ampoules (TRD P.8.3.01_020905367_07) and vials (TRD P.8.3.01_022943400_06) show a comparable behavior in “Assay” and in “Sum of all degradation products”. Statistical analysis of the Assay of the product at the recommended storage condition (5 °C) shows for the product stored in ampoules gives an estimated expiration time of 27.4 months based on the earliest crossing time from the batch 19N005. For product stored in vials the estimated expiration time is 24.9 months, based on extrapolation of Batch 20NF04 and the earliest crossing of upper Assay limit.
For these reason, all data provided, shows that the change in primary packaging does not affect the stability of Sulprostone solution 0.5 mg for injection (NALADOR) and the quality of the drug product remain unchanged.
Moreover, the approved shelf life for ampoules was maintained in vials registration for EU and RoW countries which are already approved.

Question 1
Update of the storage conditions in the product information according to Module 3.2.P.8.1 will 
be acceptable only if the statement in Module 3.2.P.8.1 itself is based on adequate stability data. 
The stability data included in this submission are inadequate to support the storage condition of 
“This medicinal product does not require any special temperature storage conditions.”. The data 
required to support this type of statement is made clear in the “Guideline on declaration of 
storage conditions (a) in the product information of medicinal products (b) for active 
substances” (CPMP/QWP/609/96/Rev 2)”, ie, data are required at both long term and 
accelerated conditions as per page 3 of this guideline. Only long term data at 25ºC / 60% RH 
have been provided; data at accelerated conditions should also be included.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (P.8.1):
Bayer would like to summarize the status and the available stability data for this product to 
support the statement on storage instruction: “The product does not require any special 
temperature storage condition.”.
The current shelf life is established for Gastrografin according to the climatic zone (cz):
- 
Countries of cz II (25ºC/60% RH): 48m.
- 
Countries of cz IVa (30ºC/65% RH) and IVb (30ºC/75% RH): 24m.
For both climatic zones, the following existing stability studies are available supporting the 
established shelf life and the statement on storage condition:
- 
P.8.3.01-03: One batch at 25ºC/60% RH (60m), 30ºC/65% RH (60m) and 40ºC/75% 
RH (6m) + three batches at 30ºC/75% RH (36m).
- 
P.8.3.901-04: Three batches at 25ºC/60% RH (60m), 30ºC/75% RH (60m) and 
40ºC/75% RH (6m).
- 
P.8.3.02-07: Five batches at 25ºC/60% RH (48m)
In addition, stability data is available for one additional batch stored at 30ºC/75% RH (60m) 
and 40ºC/75% RH (6m). So far, this data is only reported in Bayer internal documents.
The manufacturing site continues running ongoing stability studies at 25ºC/60% RH in a yearly 
basis, following GMP Guideline. As well, ongoing stability studies at 30ºC/75% RH. This 
storage condition is a “worst case” and is used to support data for cz IVa (30ºC/65% RH) and 
IVb (30ºC/75% RH).
Document P.8.1.02-03 which applies for Gastrografin Shelf life for the cz I/II (48m), III (24m), 
IVa & IVb (24m) establishes storage conditions as follows: “The product does not require any 
special temperature storage condition” and “Protect from light”
In relation to the sentence, “The product does not require any special temperature storage 
condition”, we can confirm that it is based on the EMA Guideline CPMP/QWP/609/96/Rev 2
(page 3). This Guideline establishes: Testing conditions when the product is stable, 25ºC/60% 
RH and 40ºC/75% RH, the required labelling statement is “None”, that means for the SPC and 
PL the statement “This medicinal product does not require any special storage condition” can 
be used. 
 
From our point of view the sentence related to the storage conditions could remain in the 
P.8.1.02-03 section based on the rationale above.

Please provide further documents about the risk assessment of elemental impurities to justify the rational of potential elemental impurity assessment for API and excipients only. Without the justification, the applicant is suggested to re-evaluate the risk of elemental impurities.

Since the risk assessment of elemental impurities is done via the component approach (acc. to ICH Q3D), testing and additional control of elemental impurities is not needed for drug product, therefore no testing on commercial DP samples for batches in the past 3 years can be provided. As part of the supportive data, we randomly took 3 batches and conduct the elemental impurity test on DP, the results are added in P.5.4.11-01.
In addition, please find the description of testing procedure and validation report (P.5.3.08-02) of the method used for the risk assessment in P.5.5.05-02.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Manufacturing process: Please clarify if there is batch mixing in DS manufacturing process 
and FB manufacturing process. Please clarify how many batches can be mixed and the mixing 
principal. The mixing process validation should be provided.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.S.2, 3.2.P.3):
Aflibercept drug substance intermediate (DSI) is further purified to produce drug substance 
(DS) which is then formulated to generate aflibercept formulated bulk (FB). FB is then filled 
to yield aflibercept drug product (DP). Each individual batch of the resulting material (DSI, 
DS, FB and DP) are tested and released according to specifications.

The option to pool DSI lots to manufacture DS and to pool DS lots as starting material for the 
FB manufacturing process are part of the process and are included in the master batch records 
since the initial approval of the vial presentation. Per the master batch records, operators are 
permitted to mix:
• 
Up to two DSI lots to produce one DS lot 
• 
Up to two DS lots to produce one FB lot

Therefore, a typical batch of DS or FB may originate from the same or different DSI or DS 
batches, respectively, provided the individual source DSI or DS batches meet all release 
criteria. If differing lots are combined, a protein concentration sample is performed after 
combination and mixing to inform the next operating steps.

Mixing of two DSI lots to produce a DS lot doesn’t routinely occur. Mixing of two DSI lots to 
produce one DS lot may occur based on the availability of DSI lots. Only released DSI lots, 
that have met all acceptance criteria, can be combined for further processing.

Mixing of two DS lots to produce a FB lot doesn’t routinely occur. Mixing of two DS lots to 
produce one FB lot may occur based on the availability of DS lots. Only released DS lots, 
that have met all acceptance criteria, can be combined for further processing.

Separate mixing studies to support pooling multiple DSI lots for the manufacture of DS were 
not required. During the manufacturing of DS, individual bottles of DSI, regardless of the lot 
of material in the bottle, are thawed and pooled per defined process perimeters. Separate 
mixing studies to support pooling multiple DS lots for the manufacture of FB were not 
required as mixing time and mixing speed were evaluated within the operational ranges as 
part of the full-scale process validation. All quality and performance parameters evaluated 
during the PPQ batches were consistent. Additionally, for the FB manufacturing process: the 
thawing, post-dilution, and post-excipient addition mixing time and speed are included in the 
IPC program as a general process parameter and therefore, are well controlled by 
manufacturing batch records and procedures.

The quality of drug product resulting from mixing different DSI and/or DS batches is ensured, 
in addition to the drug product release specifications (see CTD Section 3.2.P.5.1), by the DSI 
and/or DS from each individual lot as well as the resulting mixed DS and/or FB being held to 
release specifications (see CTD Sections 3.2.S.2.4 and 3.2.P.3.4). Only released DSI and DS 
lots, that have met all acceptance criteria, can be combined for further processing. All 
produced batches are held to the same quality standard of release and stability acceptance 
criteria, regardless of the number of source lots utilized.
.

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
Please clarify that: In the water (pH=5) extraction and isopropanol/water mixture extraction 
studies, there are compounds detected 3-fold above level detected in blank injection and at or 
above AET. However, why there are no compounds detected above AET in the following 
Migration Studies?
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 (3.2.P.2):
The sample solution used for the extraction study was different to the DP solution in the 
migration study.
The extraction study did use more harsh conditions to identify compounds potentially being 
released from the container material and migrating into the drug product during storage. As 
clarified in TRD 2.4.6 extraction study, the rubber components were exposed to stress 
conditions to identify what chemical species can be extracted from the container materials.
The container closure components were extracted with water adjusted to pH = 5 and with 
isopropanol/water mixture, respectively. Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL in prefilled syringe 
(PFS) is an aqueous solution of pH 6.2. Acidic pH promotes mobilization of most elemental 
impurities. An isopropanol/water mixture facilitates the migration of organic compounds into 
the solution. These conditions favor the extraction of extraneous compounds and help identify 
any species that might be migrating from the container materials.
However, for migration study, the purpose is to evaluate the potential compounds originating 
from the final container closure system (CCS) leaching into drug product for the package of 
PFS. The sample for the migration study is the drug product and it is to be expected that the 
compounds detected in the extraction study will not generally be presented in the study of 
migration study. With the latter, it was demonstrated that there are no leachable compounds 
actually migrating from the packaging materials into the drug product.
